1.why: Pressure grows directly with depth, so doubling the depth doubles the pressure.

wrong.a: Pressure increases with depth, it does not stay the same.
wrong.c: Pressure increases, it does not halve.
wrong.d: Pressure is highest at the bottom, not zero.

2.why: In hydrostatic pressure, ρ stands for fluid density in kg/m³.

wrong.c: Height or depth is represented by h.
wrong.d: Power is not in this equation.

3.why: Water pressure is much greater at the bottom, requiring thicker walls to hold it back.

wrong.a: Wall thickness is for strength, not saving concrete.
wrong.b: Air temperature does not change wall thickness needs.
wrong.d: Dam walls are not built for catching fish.

_quiz_pool.question: What happens to water pressure as you go deeper in a lake?
_quiz_pool.explanation: The weight of more water above increases the pressure.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of pressure in SI?
In p = ρ × g × h, what does h represent?
_quiz_pool.explanation: h is the depth below the fluid surface in metres.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the density of pure water (ρ)?
Why do deep-sea submarines need very strong hulls?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Deep water exerts immense hydrostatic pressure.

_quiz_pool.question: If depth is tripled, how does hydrostatic pressure change?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Pressure is directly proportional to depth h.

_quiz_pool.question: What force pulls water downward in a reservoir?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Gravity pulls mass down, creating weight and pressure.

_quiz_pool.question: Which of these is a primary source for water and earth science?
_quiz_pool.explanation: USGS provides scientific data and water monitoring reports.

_quiz_pool.question: Does water pressure push only downward?
options: No, it pushes in all directions
_quiz_pool.explanation: Fluid pressure acts equally in all directions at a given depth.

_quiz_pool.question: What is standard gravity g used in these calculations?

must_show: an empty plastic bottle with multiple holes at different heights
water squirting out of the holes
a ruler or measuring surface showing jet distance
safety: no flame, no hot water, no electricity
_lab_rubric.pass_if: The photos show water squirting further from the lower hole due to greater pressure.

cover.title: How water pressure builds
cover.subtitle: Water pushes down with heavy force as you go deeper. Discover how pressure grows underwater and why deep structures need tough walls.
cover.subject: Physics · Pressure
cover.fun_fact: Water pressure increases by about 9,800 pascals for every single metre of depth.
story.title: Deep water and hidden force
story.lead: Rain and river runoff fill lakes and reservoirs across the region [1]. As water collects in deep basins, the pressure at the bottom rises significantly [2].
story.image_caption: Archive photo · Three buffaloes heads above water in Si Phan Don
story.image_credit: Basile Morin / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
stat.1.label: water density in kg/m³
stat.2.label: gravity in m/s²
stat.3.label: depth for 98,000 Pa pressure
story.body_1: A water has mass, and Earth's gravity pulls it down. When water piles up deep in a lake or behind a dam, the layers above push down on the layers below [2]. This squeezing force is called hydrostatic pressure.
story.body_2: Engineers must design dam walls and underwater equipment to withstand this immense pressure [3]. The deeper you go, the stronger the push becomes against every square metre of surface [2].
timeline.1.text: Water pressure equals atmospheric pressure at the top.
timeline.2.text: Pressure increases as water weight above presses down.
timeline.3.text: Pressure reaches about 196,000 Pa at ten metres.
physics.title: Pressure in a fluid
physics.body_1: Hydrostatic pressure depends on three things: how dense the fluid is, how strong gravity is, and how deep you are below the surface.
physics.body_2: The equation p = ρ × g × h shows that pressure grows in a straight line with depth. Double the depth, and you double the pressure.
physics.assumptions: We assume water density is constant and ignore air pressure at the surface for the added fluid pressure.

lab.title: Water bottle jet test
lab.step_1: Poke three small holes at different heights in an empty plastic bottle.
lab.step_2: Cover the holes with tape, fill the bottle with water, and place it in a sink.
lab.step_3: Remove tape quickly and observe how far water jets shoot from each hole.
lab.question: Which hole shoots water the furthest? Explain why using the idea of depth h.

glossary.1.def: Pressure exerted by a fluid at rest due to the force of gravity.
glossary.2.def: Mass per unit volume of a substance.
glossary.3.def: The SI unit of pressure, equal to one newton per square metre.
